cox_forest() Tutorial

Julian Silan

2026-08-19

This tutorial walks through cox_forest() end to end using survival::lung, a built-in dataset of advanced lung cancer patients. It covers data preparation, a basic univariable forest plot, categorical vs. continuous covariates, custom reference levels, level exclusion, multivariable models, multiple endpoints, and the main styling arguments.

Source the function first (adjust the path to wherever cox_forest.R lives relative to this .Rmd file):

source("/Users/julian/Desktop/VHIO/R code/Forestplot/Univariable_Multivariable/cox.forest_function.R")
library(survival)
library(dplyr)

1 Prepare the data

survival::lung needs a little massaging before it’s ready for Cox modelling: status is coded 1/2 (censored/dead) rather than 0/1, sex is an unlabelled numeric code, and ph.ecog is stored as numeric even though it is really an ordered categorical performance-status score. We also add a synthetic treatment arm and a synthetic PFS endpoint so the tutorial can demonstrate multivariable models and multi-endpoint plots.

set.seed(42)

lung2 <- survival::lung %>%
  mutate(
    event_os  = status - 1,                       # 1 = death, 0 = censored
    time_os   = time,
    sex       = factor(sex, levels = c(1, 2), labels = c("Male", "Female")),
    ph.ecog   = factor(ph.ecog),                   # 0-3 performance status
    treatment = sample(c("Arm A", "Arm B"), n(), replace = TRUE),
    time_pfs  = pmin(time_os, time_os * runif(n(), 0.4, 0.9)),
    event_pfs = ifelse(time_pfs < time_os, 1, event_os)
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(ph.ecog), !is.na(sex), !is.na(age))

#glimpse(lung2)

time_pfs / event_pfs here are a simulated PFS endpoint (PFS event always occurs no later than OS) purely so the tutorial has two endpoints to work with — survival::lung does not contain real PFS data.

2 A single-covariate univariable forest plot

The simplest possible call: one categorical covariate, one endpoint, univariable model.

res_sex <- cox_forest(
  data       = lung2,
  covariates = "sex",
  labels     = "Sex",
  time       = "time_os",
  event      = "event_os",
  endpoint_labels = "OS",
  model_type = "univariable"
)

res_sex$results_table
covariate covariate_label level is_reference n n_event hr conf_low conf_high p_value endpoint endpoint_label model_type
sex Sex Male TRUE 137 111 NA NA NA NA time_os OS univariable
sex Sex Female FALSE 90 53 0.5923301 0.4266362 0.8223749 0.0017597 time_os OS univariable 
res_sex$plots$univariable

results_table has one row per covariate level — including an explicit "Reference" row for the first factor level ("Male", since that’s levels(lung2$sex)[1]) with hr/conf_low/conf_high set to NA. The plot draws no marker or CI line for that row, exactly as expected for a reference category.

3 Several covariates at once (categorical + continuous)

Add age (continuous — auto-detected because it has more than 5 distinct values) and ph.ecog (categorical, 4 levels). Each covariate still gets its own univariable Cox model: Surv(time_os, event_os) ~ age, Surv(time_os, event_os) ~ sex, Surv(time_os, event_os) ~ ph.ecog.

res_uni <- cox_forest(
  data       = lung2,
  covariates = c("sex", "age", "ph.ecog"),
  labels     = c("Sex", "Age", "ECOG PS"),
  time       = "time_os",
  event      = "event_os",
  endpoint_labels = "OS",
  continuous_vars = "age",
  model_type = "univariable"
)

res_uni$plots$univariable

3.1 Specify x-axis

res_uni <- cox_forest(
  data       = lung2,
  covariates = c("sex", "age", "ph.ecog"),
  labels     = c("Sex", "Age", "ECOG PS"),
  time       = "time_os",
  event      = "event_os",
  endpoint_labels = "OS",
  continuous_vars = "age",
  model_type = "univariable",
  xlim = c(0.25, 4),
  ticks_at = c(0.5, 1, 2),
)

res_uni$plots$univariable

For age, results_table$level reads "per 1-unit increase". To report the HR per 10-year increase instead:

res_uni_age10 <- cox_forest(
  data       = lung2,
  covariates = c("sex", "age", "ph.ecog"),
  labels     = c("Sex", "Age", "ECOG PS"),
  time       = "time_os",
  event      = "event_os",
  continuous_vars = "age",
  continuous_increase = list(age = 10),
  model_type = "univariable"
)

res_uni_age10$results_table %>% filter(covariate == "age")
covariate covariate_label level is_reference n n_event hr conf_low conf_high p_value endpoint endpoint_label model_type
age Age per 10-unit increase FALSE 227 164 1.208873 1.008797 1.448629 0.0398942 time_os time_os univariable

4 Custom reference levels

By default the reference level for a categorical covariate is its first factor level. Use ref_levels to change that — useful, for example, to make "Female" the reference for sex, or a “good” ECOG score the reference instead of "0".

res_ref <- cox_forest(
  data       = lung2,
  covariates = c("sex", "ph.ecog"),
  labels     = c("Sex", "ECOG PS"),
  time       = "time_os",
  event      = "event_os",
  ref_levels = list(sex = "Female"),
  model_type = "univariable",
  xlim = c(0.25, 4),
  ticks_at = c(0.5, 1, 2),
)

res_ref$plots$univariable

5 Excluding a level

ph.ecog == "3" has only a handful of patients in lung. exclude_levels drops it by setting those values to NA, which then falls out through the existing complete-case filtering used inside each model:

res_excl <- cox_forest(
  data       = lung2,
  covariates = c("sex", "ph.ecog"),
  labels     = c("Sex", "ECOG PS"),
  time       = "time_os",
  event      = "event_os",
  exclude_levels = list(ph.ecog = "3"),
  model_type = "univariable"
)

res_excl$results_table %>% filter(covariate == "ph.ecog")
covariate covariate_label level is_reference n n_event hr conf_low conf_high p_value endpoint endpoint_label model_type
ph.ecog ECOG PS 0 TRUE 63 37 NA NA NA NA time_os time_os univariable
ph.ecog ECOG PS 1 FALSE 113 82 1.445768 0.9794896 2.134014 0.0635040 time_os time_os univariable
ph.ecog ECOG PS 2 FALSE 50 44 2.497529 1.6082942 3.878427 0.0000458 time_os time_os univariable

For a multivariable model this exclusion drops the affected patients from the entire model (since multivariable fitting requires complete cases across every covariate simultaneously) — see the next section.

6 Multivariable models

Setting model_type = "multivariable" fits one Cox model containing all requested covariates together: Surv(time_os, event_os) ~ sex + age + ph.ecog.

res_multi <- cox_forest(
  data       = lung2,
  covariates = c("sex", "age", "ph.ecog"),
  labels     = c("Sex", "Age", "ECOG PS"),
  time       = "time_os",
  event      = "event_os",
  continuous_vars = "age",
  model_type = "multivariable",
  xlim = c(0.25, 4),
  ticks_at = c(0.5, 1, 2),
)

res_multi$plots$multivariable

To see univariable and multivariable side by side (e.g. for a “crude vs adjusted” supplementary table), request both:

res_both <- cox_forest(
  data       = lung2,
  covariates = c("sex", "age", "ph.ecog"),
  labels     = c("Sex", "Age", "ECOG PS"),
  time       = "time_os",
  event      = "event_os",
  continuous_vars = "age",
  model_type = "both"
)

res_both$plots$univariable

res_both$plots$multivariable

7 Including a treatment / arm variable

There’s nothing special about a treatment arm — add it to covariates (and labels) exactly like any other covariate:

res_trt <- cox_forest(
  data       = lung2,
  covariates = c("treatment", "sex", "age", "ph.ecog"),
  labels     = c("Treatment", "Sex", "Age", "ECOG PS"),
  time       = "time_os",
  event      = "event_os",
  continuous_vars = "age",
  ref_levels = list(treatment = "Arm A"),
  model_type = "multivariable",
  xlim = c(0.25, 4),
  ticks_at = c(0.5, 1, 2),
)

res_trt$plots$multivariable

8 Multiple endpoints (OS and PFS) with colour coding

Pass time and event as vectors, paired by position, along with matching endpoint_labels. With more than one endpoint the plot automatically colour-codes the confidence intervals per endpoint and adds a legend below the figure.

res_two_ep <- cox_forest(
  data       = lung2,
  covariates = c("treatment", "sex", "age"),
  labels     = c("Treatment", "Sex", "Age"),
  time       = c("time_os", "time_pfs"),
  event      = c("event_os", "event_pfs"),
  endpoint_labels = c("OS", "PFS"),
  continuous_vars = "age",
  ref_levels = list(treatment = "Arm A"),
  model_type = "univariable",
  palette    = c("#1B9E77", "#D95F02")   # one colour per endpoint
)

res_two_ep$plots$univariable

Rows are grouped covariate-major (all OS/PFS rows for Treatment together, then all rows for Sex, then Age), so each covariate’s cross-endpoint comparison stays visually adjacent.

9 Styling the plot

A few of the most commonly adjusted arguments:

res_styled <- cox_forest(
  data       = lung2,
  covariates = c("treatment", "sex", "ph.ecog"),
  labels     = c("Treatment", "Sex", "ECOG PS"),
  time       = "time_os",
  event      = "event_os",
  ref_levels = list(treatment = "Arm A"),
  model_type = "univariable",
  digits      = 2,
  row_height  = 1.4,                    # 40% taller rows
  ci_pch      = 15,                     # rectangle markers
  ci_lwd      = 3,                      # thickness of the lines
  ci_Theight = 0.6,                     # height of CI bands
  sizes       = 1,                      # size of HR
  risk_labels = c("Favours Arm A", "Favours Arm B"),
  title       = "Univariable Cox regression - Overall Survival",
  covariate_label_row = TRUE            # bold header row per covariate
)

res_styled$plots$univariable

  • row_height — multiplier applied to every body row’s height (1.3 = 30% taller); useful when labels wrap or the figure feels cramped.
  • covariate_label_row = TRUE inserts a dedicated bold row with just the covariate name above its levels, instead of bolding the first level row in place.
  • risk_labels adds directional arrow annotations under the x-axis (only makes sense when every covariate shares a consistent “favours A / favours B” framing, e.g. a single treatment-arm-anchored subgroup plot).
  • xlim / ticks_at let you fix the axis range and tick marks manually instead of relying on the automatic (CI-range-based) defaults — handy for keeping several related figures on the same scale.

10 Adopt length of the forestplot

res_length <- cox_forest(
  data       = lung2,
  covariates = c("treatment", "sex", "ph.ecog"),
  labels     = c("Treatment", "Sex", "ECOG PS"),
  time       = "time_os",
  event      = "event_os",
  ref_levels = list(treatment = "Arm A"),
  model_type = "univariable",
  xlim       = c(0.25, 4),
  ticks_at   = c( 0.5, 1, 2),
  digits      = 2,
  row_height  = 1.3,                    # 30% taller rows
  ci_pch      = 18,                     # diamond markers
  ci_lwd      = 2,
  sizes       = 1,                      # size of HR
  length_plot = 60,
  risk_labels = c("Favours Arm A", "Favours Arm B"),
  title       = "Univariable Cox regression - Overall Survival",
  covariate_label_row = TRUE            # bold header row per covariate
)

res_length$plots$univariable
